items.title: Ecuador doubles tariffs on Colombia to 100% as trade war deepens

featured_image.name: Ecuador raises tariffs on Colombia to 100% from 50% | The Star

items.description:
Ecuador announced on Thursday that it will raise tariffs on all imports from Colombia to 100 percent, effective May 1, in the latest and most dramatic escalation of a trade war between the two Andean neighbors that has been building since January.[1][2]

The government cited Colombia's "failure to implement concrete and effective border security measures" as justification for the increase, framing the levy as a sovereign response to drug trafficking along their shared border. "This measure is based on national security criteria and seeks to reinforce shared responsibility in a task that must be undertaken jointly to address the presence of drug trafficking at the border," the Ministry of Production, Foreign Trade, and Investment said in a statement.[2][1]

items.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to 32-hour Orthodox Easter ceasefire

featured_image.name: Putin announces Orthodox Easter ceasefire after rejecting Ukraine's proposal

items.description:
Russia and Ukraine have agreed to observe a 32-hour ceasefire over the Orthodox Easter weekend, with Russian President Vladimir Putin ordering his forces to halt combat operations "in all directions" starting Saturday, according to a Kremlin statement issued Thursday. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who had been pushing for such a truce for more than a week, agreed to the pause.[1][2][3]

The ceasefire is set to begin at 4 p.m. Moscow time (1 p.m. GMT) on Saturday, April 11, and will last through the end of Easter Sunday, April 12. Defense Minister Andrei Belousov and Chief of the General Staff Valery Gerasimov have been instructed to halt all military operations during the period.[4][5][6][7]

items.title: MIT develops silent artificial muscle fibers for robots

featured_image.name: MIT's fiber-based artificial muscles can lift 650 times their own weight

items.description: Researchers at the MIT Media Lab and Politecnico di Bari in Italy have developed a new class of artificial muscle fibers that operate silently and without motors, external pumps, or bulky hydraulic equipment — a breakthrough that could reshape how robots move and how wearable assistive devices are built.

items.title: Trump says he's 'very optimistic' about Iran deal as Vance heads to Islamabad

featured_image.name: WH Briefing Iran 4/6/26

items.description:
President Donald Trump said Thursday he was "very optimistic" about reaching a peace deal with Iran, even as a two-day-old ceasefire showed signs of strain over continued Israeli strikes in Lebanon and disputes about the status of the Strait of Hormuz.

In a telephone interview with NBC News, Trump said Iranian leaders were "much more reasonable" in private negotiations than in their public statements, but warned that "if they don't make a deal, it's going to be very painful."[1][2]

items.title: Starmer, Trump discuss plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: President Trump’s ceasefire with Iran draws praise from world leaders

items.description: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer spoke with President Donald Trump on Thursday evening about developing a practical plan to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, calling from Qatar during a tour of the Gulf region aimed at shoring up the fragile ceasefire between the United States and Iran.

items.title: Trump demands Iran stop charging tolls on Hormuz strait

featured_image.name: Vessels pass through Strait of Hormuz following US-Iran ceasefire

items.description: President Donald Trump on Thursday demanded that Iran cease imposing fees on oil tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz, writing on Truth Social that "They better not be and, if they are, they better stop now!" The warning further strained a fragile two-week ceasefire between Washington and Tehran, agreed to just two days earlier, under which Iran was supposed to fully reopen the critical waterway.[1][2]

items.title: Forecasters warn potential super El Nino could reshape global weather by late 2026

featured_image.name: India's monsoon will worsen: Ocean's salt could be making El Nino ...

items.description: Climate scientists and forecasting agencies are sounding alarms over what could become one of the strongest El Niño events in modern history, with models pointing toward a potential super El Niño developing in the second half of 2026 that would reshape weather patterns from India to California.

items.title: OpenAI pitches compute edge over Anthropic as revenue gap widens

featured_image.name: Anthropic, OpenAI rivalry spills into new Super Bowl ads as both fight to win over AI users

items.description:
OpenAI told investors this week that its early investments in computing infrastructure give it a key advantage over rival Anthropic at a moment when the smaller company is gaining ground in revenue and mulling a public offering, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday.[1][2]

The pitch comes as OpenAI faces mounting pressure from Anthropic, which disclosed on April 7 that its annualized revenue run rate has surpassed $30 billion — up from $9 billion at the end of 2025 and now exceeding OpenAI's most recently reported $25 billion figure. The number of Anthropic business customers spending more than $1 million annually has doubled from 500 in February to 1,000.[3][4][5]

items.title: Oil prices rebound as Iran accuses U.S. of ceasefire breach

featured_image.name: Tankers showing caution around Strait of Hormuz after attack on Iran

items.description: A doubling of jet fuel prices since the outbreak of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran in late February has forced airlines worldwide to slash flights, raise fares, and hike baggage fees — reshaping the economics of air travel just as the summer season approaches. A fragile two-week ceasefire announced on Wednesday offered a glimmer of relief, but carriers are signaling that higher costs for travelers are here to stay.

items.title: Iran's Khamenei vows revenge, signals 'new phase' at Hormuz

featured_image.name: Resolute to take revenge for late Supreme Leader, martyrs: Mojtaba ...

items.description: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei declared on Thursday that Tehran would seek retribution for attacks on the country and move the management of the Strait of Hormuz into a "new phase," delivering a defiant message that threatens to upend a fragile ceasefire with the United States just days before critical peace talks in Pakistan.

items.title: Trump says he's 'very optimistic' on Iran deal amid Lebanon crisis

featured_image.name: Trump allies play down Iran 'genocide' threats as critics warn of war crimes

items.description:
President Trump said Thursday he was "very optimistic" about securing a peace deal with Iran, even as massive Israeli strikes on Lebanon threatened to unravel a fragile ceasefire between Washington and Tehran that is only days old.

In a telephone interview with NBC News, Trump said Iranian leaders were "much more reasonable" in private negotiations than in their public statements, according to AFP. He added a warning: "If they don't make a deal, it's going to be very painful".[1][2]

items.title: Netanyahu rejects cease-fire calls, vows strikes on Hezbollah

featured_image.name: Israeli attacks across Lebanon kill at least 254 after Iran-US ceasefire

items.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reiterated on Thursday that there is no ceasefire in Lebanon, defying international calls to extend a fragile US-Iran truce to cover Israeli military operations against Hezbollah. In a video message, Netanyahu declared, "There is no ceasefire. We are continuing to hit Hezbollah with force and we will not stop until we restore security," while also directing his cabinet to pursue direct negotiations with the Lebanese government aimed at disarming the militant group.[1]

The statement came a day after Israel carried out its deadliest wave of strikes on Lebanon since the broader conflict began in early March, with the Israeli military saying it hit more than 100 Hezbollah command centers and military sites across Beirut, the Bekaa Valley, and southern Lebanon in just 10 minutes. Lebanon's health ministry reported at least 254 people killed and over 1,165 wounded in Wednesday's attacks, according to Al Jazeera. Several strikes hit densely populated commercial and residential areas in central Beirut without prior warning.[2][3][4][5][6]

items.title: Iran envoy deletes post on Islamabad delegation amid ceasefire rift

featured_image.name: What to Know About Iran’s Ceasefire Proposal as Peace Talks Approach

items.description:
Iran's Ambassador to Pakistan, Reza Amiri Moghadam, deleted a post on X late Thursday announcing that an Iranian delegation would arrive in Islamabad that evening for talks with the United States, raising fresh uncertainty about whether high-stakes negotiations set for Friday will go ahead as planned.

Moghadam had written that "despite skepticism of Iranian public opinion due to repeated ceasefire violations by Israeli regime to sabotage the diplomatic initiative," the delegation would arrive Thursday night at the invitation of Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for "serious talks based on 10 points proposed by Iran," according to Moneycontrol, which published the text of the post before it was removed. The post was subsequently deleted, Xinhua International reported, though no official explanation was given.[1][2]

items.title: Iran demands Bitcoin tolls for Hormuz tanker passage

featured_image.name: Oil Tanker Collision Near Strait of Hormuz Raises Security ...

items.description: Despite a two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran announced Tuesday evening, Tehran is pressing ahead with demands that oil tankers pay tolls in Bitcoin and other digital currencies to transit the Strait of Hormuz, raising doubts about whether the critical waterway will see a meaningful return of commercial shipping anytime soon.

items.title: UK forces Russian submarines to retreat from undersea cables

featured_image.name: MPs warned Russia is way ahead in undersea warfare

items.description:
Britain on Thursday revealed it had tracked three Russian submarines conducting covert operations near undersea cables and pipelines in waters north of the UK, in a month-long surveillance campaign that ended with all three vessels retreating toward Russia.

Defence Secretary John Healey said British forces identified an Akula-class nuclear attack submarine entering international waters in the High North several weeks ago and quickly determined it was deployed as a distraction while two submarines from Russia's Main Directorate of Deep Sea Research, known as GUGI, carried out what the Ministry of Defence described as "nefarious activity" near critical underwater infrastructure.[1]

items.title: Iran's nuclear chief rejects enrichment curbs ahead of Islamabad talks

featured_image.name: Iran's atomic chief says uranium enrichment Teheran's red line

items.description:
Iran's nuclear chief Mohammad Eslami on Thursday dismissed demands to curtail the country's uranium enrichment program, calling such efforts futile just days before high-stakes negotiations with the United States are set to begin in Pakistan's capital.

Speaking on the sidelines of a memorial service marking 40 days since the death of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Eslami said that "the claims and demands of our enemies to restrict Iran's enrichment programme are merely wishes that will be buried," according to Iran's ISNA news agency. He added that no law or external pressure could halt Iran's nuclear progress and that demands to abandon enrichment were "nonsensical".[1][2][3]

items.title: Netanyahu orders direct peace talks with Lebanon on Hezbollah

featured_image.name: Netanyahu agrees to join Trump’s Gaza Board of Peace after initial pushback

items.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced Thursday that he had instructed his cabinet to begin direct negotiations with Lebanon "as soon as possible," a move that marks a reversal after Israel previously rebuffed Lebanese overtures for talks.[1][2]

"In light of Lebanon's repeated requests to open direct negotiations with Israel, I instructed the cabinet yesterday to start direct negotiations with Lebanon as soon as possible," Netanyahu said in a statement, according to Reuters. The negotiations would focus on "disarming Hezbollah and establishing peaceful relations between Israel and Lebanon," he added.[3][1]

items.title: Trump demands European warships in Hormuz within days

featured_image.name: Trump claims coalition to send war ships to reopen strait of Hormuz

items.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz is insisting that any German military involvement in securing the Strait of Hormuz must come under an international mandate, setting up a diplomatic standoff with President Donald Trump, who has issued what European diplomats describe as an ultimatum demanding allied warships in the waterway within days.

items.title: Oil prices climb again as Strait of Hormuz stays shut despite ceasefire

featured_image.name: Iran confirms seizure of oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz

items.description: The two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran, announced on April 7, has done little to settle global energy and commodity markets, as the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed and oil prices have begun climbing again after an initial sharp selloff.

items.title: Finland nears launch of world's first permanent nuclear waste site

featured_image.name: Finland's plan to bury spent nuclear fuel for 100,000 years

items.description: After more than two decades of construction, Finland's Onkalo facility is set to become the first site on Earth to permanently dispose of spent nuclear fuel, with authorities expected to grant an operating license within months, according to the Associated Press.[1]
